payload.title: AI Builders Daily · 2026-09-01
payload.summary:
**Codex** keeps pulling product talent into orbit as **Nan Yu** joins **OpenAI** and **Thibault Sottiaux** openly asks what still blocks adoption; **Guillermo Rauch** pushes two sharp claims at once, turning Markdown into a design-system weapon and token budgets into infra governance; **Aaron Levie** calls a new phase for enterprise AI, where companies with serious data can train their own models while open models race closer in cyber; **Rich Sutton** throws cold water on synthetic-data optimism and drags the conversation back to continual learning in a world that never stops changing.

**Codex** 这边还在加速招人，**Nan Yu** 转去 **OpenAI** 做 **Codex** 和 **ChatGPT**，**Thibault Sottiaux** 则直接追问大家到底还在卡什么；**Guillermo Rauch** 连发两枪，一边说 Markdown 可以管住设计品味，一边把 token 预算说成基础设施治理问题；**Aaron Levie** 盯上企业自训模型这条线，觉得有数据的公司终于能自己下场，另一边开源模型在安全场景里也追得很凶；**Rich Sutton** 还是那个路数，直接泼冷水，不太买合成数据那套，话题又被他拽回“持续学习”这个老问题上。

sections.headline: **Rich Sutton** says learning never stopped being continual / **Rich Sutton** 直说：学习本来就该是持续的
sections.body:
In **Training Data**, **Rich Sutton** and **Khurram Javed** argue that the field drifted into a strange habit of treating “continual learning” as a niche, when real learning never turns off. Sutton restates the **Bitter Lesson** in blunt terms: stop stuffing systems with human priors and build methods that scale with computation. He sees **LLMs** as both proof and warning, powerful because they scaled on internet data, but boxed in once that finite corpus runs dry. On synthetic data, he is even sharper: from the **big world hypothesis** view, fabricated examples do not solve the fact that the world still contains far more to learn.

在 **Training Data** 这期里，**Rich Sutton** 和 **Khurram Javed** 的意思很直白：把“持续学习”当成一个特殊分支，本身就有点跑偏，学习哪有暂停键。Sutton 又把 **Bitter Lesson** 讲了一遍，不过这次更不客气了：别老想着往系统里硬塞人的经验，去做那些真能跟着算力放大的方法。按他的说法，**LLM** 既是正例也是反例，靠吃下互联网语料确实冲得很猛，但互联网终归是有限的，吃完就会撞墙。至于合成数据，他更不留情，从 **big world hypothesis** 的角度看，伪造更多样本不等于解决问题，世界里还有一大堆没学到的东西。

sections.headline: PMs need frontier-model judgment, not just roadmap polish / 现在的 PM 得真懂模型边界，不只是会排路线图
sections.body:
If you’re a PM, there is immense alpha in understanding the model frontier for your specific product and use cases.

You should be able to answer the following better than most frontier lab researchers and PMs for your use cases:

1/ What can models in each size category do well today?

2/ Where does each model fail?

3/ What workarounds can you use to overcome these failures ?

4/ Given the trajectory, what will these models likely be able to do 2–3 months from now? How should your roadmap look given this?

This is a core part of the PM job now.

如果你是 PM，真正理解适用于你产品和场景的模型前沿，里面有很大的 alpha。

对于你自己的场景，下面这些问题你应该比大多数前沿实验室研究员和 PM 回答得更清楚：

1/ 现在各个体量的模型分别擅长什么？

2/ 每个模型会栽在哪些地方？

3/ 你能用什么 workaround 去绕开这些问题？

4/ 按现在这条线往前看，2 到 3 个月后这些模型大概率会多出哪些能力？基于这个，你的路线图该怎么排？

这已经是 PM 工作里很核心的一部分了。

sections.headline: Token budgets are infrastructure governance / token 预算本质上就是基础设施治理
sections.body:
Coding tokens are basically infrastructure. Yet, the way companies have approached them amounts to:

"Hey all, here's an AWS key. It can spin up anything from a 𝚝𝟹.𝚗𝚊𝚗𝚘 (＄𝟹.𝟾𝟶/𝚖𝚘) to an 𝚙𝟻.𝟺𝟾𝚡𝚕𝚊𝚛𝚐𝚎 (＄𝟺𝟶𝚔/𝚖𝚘). Go wild"

And obviously the reason companies don't do this for their core infra is that you need to govern, optimize, and observe usage and costs.

The intern might decide to host a static website in that 192 vCPU machine, and you won't be very happy about the bill.

AI Gateway fixes this for all your tokens, with per-key, and now per-user budgets.

写代码用的 token，本质上就是基础设施。可很多公司现在的做法，差不多等于：

“各位，这是一个 **AWS** key。它能随便拉机器，从 𝚝𝟹.𝚗𝚊𝚗𝚘（＄𝟹.𝟾𝟶/𝚖𝚘）到 𝚙𝟻.𝟺𝟾𝚡𝚕𝚊𝚛𝚐𝚎（＄𝟺𝟶𝚔/𝚖𝚘），想怎么开就怎么开。”

公司显然不会这么管核心基础设施，因为你得治理、优化，还得盯住使用情况和成本。

不然实习生哪天心血来潮，把一个静态网站丢到那台 192 vCPU 机器上，月底账单出来你肯定笑不出来。

**AI Gateway** 现在就在补这个坑，给所有 token 加上按 key、现在还支持按用户的预算控制。

sections.headline: More companies may train their own models now / 手里有数据的公司，自己训模型这件事开始像真选项了
sections.body:
Now that the base open weights AI models are getting far better, and post training infra is becoming more mature and commercialized, there are going to be all new plays for companies that have large amounts of data to have their own models.

Licensing data for external model training was previously the only play if you had a large corpus of information, but you can now reasonably go and train your own models as well without incurring the cost and complexity of competing with the labs on research.

The general purpose frontier models will still have a leg up in broad areas due to the ability to handle the widest set of tasks, but you can absolutely see a future where we have far more models than today across every vertical and domain.

现在基础开源权重模型强了很多，后训练基础设施也越来越成熟、越来越商业化，所以对那些手里握着大量数据的公司来说，围绕“自有模型”会冒出一批全新的打法。

以前如果你有一大坨高价值语料，基本只有一条路，就是把数据授权给外部做模型训练；但现在你也完全可以认真考虑自己训练模型，而且不需要承担和那些实验室拼研究的成本与复杂度。

通用型前沿模型在很多宽场景上还是会领先，毕竟它们能覆盖最广的一组任务；但你完全能想见一个未来，到时候各个垂直领域、各个行业里的模型数量都会比今天多得多。

sections.headline: Anthropomorphism helps until it turns into panic theater / 拟人化有用，但别拿它来煽动恐慌
sections.body:
Anthropomorphization of AI is good when it serves to help us use (understand, predict, etc) AI better. 

It’s bad when it serves to sow panic, fear, and unrealistic / unwarranted comparisons to human beings. 

Most opponents of anthropomorphism are rightly reacting to its misuse to sow panic or alter the moral status of agents by claiming consciousness etc. 

It’s possible to use anthropomorphism without doing that though

当 AI 的拟人化能帮我们更好地使用它、理解它、预测它的时候，这件事是有好处的。

但如果它只是用来制造恐慌、放大恐惧，或者硬把 AI 跟人做不现实、也站不住脚的类比，那就坏了。

很多反对拟人化的人，其实主要是在反感它被滥用，比如拿“意识”这种说法来煽动恐慌，或者硬抬高 agent 的道德地位。

不过，拟人化并不是只能这么用。
